subject: geography
title: Sustainable Cities & Urban Form
meta_desc: A-Level Geography adventure on sustainable urban design, BedZED, Curitiba and Masdar.
final_note: Sustainable cities balance social, economic and environmental goals.

concepts.def: Meets present needs without compromising future generations; low carbon, equitable.
Beddington Zero Energy Development, London (2002): 100 homes carbon-neutral by design.
Brazilian city with BRT system carrying 2 million passengers/day; recycling 70 percent of waste.
Abu Dhabi planned eco-city aiming for net-zero; uses solar and pedestrian-only design.
Bus Rapid Transit; dedicated lanes mimic light rail at lower cost.
Spatial pattern of land use; compact, polycentric or sprawl.

walkthroughs.body_html: BedZED (Sutton, London 2002) houses 220 residents in 100 homes. Designed by Bill Dunster for Peabody Trust. Uses 2/3 less energy than average UK home; achieves 81 percent reduction in hot water energy use. Triple glazing, super-insulation, south-facing.

Curitiba's BRT (since 1974) carries 2 million passengers/day; mayor Jaime Lerner pioneered linear development corridors. Green space increased from 1 m^2/person (1970) to 52 m^2/person today. Recycling: 70 percent of household waste sorted.

Masdar (Abu Dhabi 2008) aimed for net-zero but downsized targets after 2008 crisis. 10 MW solar PV, driverless PRT pods, pedestrian streets. Population reached only 5000 of planned 50000 by 2023, raising questions about top-down eco-design.
